dialogue.scene: Omar and his sister Reem are talking about a new football video game at home.

p1.t: Omar, that's three hours on that game! What do you think about your screen time today?
To be honest, it's a bit too much. But this new football game is really addictive.
In my opinion, three hours is a waste of time. It's a beautiful day outside.
Maybe, but it isn't a complete waste. I'm learning to work with my team online.

p2.t: That's interesting. What do you think about playing real football instead?
Well, I think real football is better for my health, because I actually move.
Exactly. So let's go to the park after Asr. Dad can take us.
Fine! I'll save the game and come with you.

dialogue.focus: I think real football is better for my health, because I actually move.
qs: Why does Reem think three hours of gaming is a waste of time?
What does Omar think about real football?

speakout.scene: Your school magazine is asking students: should children have a daily screen-time limit? I'm a reporter, and I want to interview you.

prompts.q: What do you think about having a daily screen-time limit?
prompts.hint: Start with 'I think' or 'In my opinion' and give one reason with 'because'.

prompts.q: Which games or apps are a waste of time, in your opinion?
prompts.hint: Name one and explain why you think so.

prompts.q: And what do your parents think about your screen time?

qs: What do you think about esports? Is it a real sport?
In your opinion, what is a good screen-time rule for families?

0-0.exit: Give me your opinion about video games in two sentences, and use 'because' in one of them.

dialogue.scene: Noura and her classmate Sara are in the school canteen at break time.

p1.t: Noura, what's your opinion of the new canteen menu?
Personally, I'm not keen on it. The pasta was tasteless yesterday.
Really? I liked the chicken wrap. I believe it's a healthy option too.
Maybe, but they stopped selling samosas! That's a real shame.

p2.t: In my opinion, it's good that they sell less fried food.
I suppose so. But I believe students should be able to choose.
What do you think about writing to the head teacher about it?
That's a great idea! Let's ask her to add fresh juice and dates.

dialogue.focus: I believe students should be able to choose.
qs: Why isn't Noura keen on the new menu?
What do the girls want to ask the head teacher to add?

speakout.scene: Your school wants to change the canteen menu. I'm the head teacher, and I'd like to hear your opinion before we decide.

prompts.q: What's your opinion of the food in our canteen?

prompts.q: Do you believe we should stop selling sweets and fizzy drinks?
prompts.hint: Say 'I believe that …' and give a reason.

points: In Japan, students often serve lunch to their classmates and clean up afterwards.

qs: What do you think about students serving lunch, like in Japan?
In your opinion, should schools give free lunch to every student?

0-1.exit: Tell me your opinion of your school food in two sentences. Start one of them with 'Personally'.

dialogue.scene: Faisal and his cousin Sam have just watched an animated film at a cinema in Jeddah.

p1.t: So, Faisal, what did you think of the film?
I found it really funny, but the plot was a bit confusing in the middle.
Really? I thought the plot was clever. The ending surprised me.
True, the ending was great. But was the first film better?

p2.t: To be honest, I think the first one is a bit overrated. This one was better.
I'm not sure. How do you feel about films with so many songs?
I usually skip the songs at home! But overall, it was worth watching.
In my opinion, it's the best film this year. Let's tell everyone at school!

dialogue.focus: I found it really funny, but the plot was a bit confusing in the middle.
qs: What did Faisal find confusing?
What does Sam think about the first film?

speakout.scene: You've just watched a film or series that everyone is talking about. I'm your friend, and I haven't seen it yet.

prompts.q: What did you think of it?

prompts.hint: Describe the character and say if you liked them.

prompts.q: Is it worth watching, or is it overrated?

dialogue.scene: Khalid and his friend Daniel, who lives in Riyadh, are watching Al-Hilal play Al-Nassr on TV.

p1.t: That was never a penalty! The referee made a terrible mistake.
If you ask me, it was a penalty. The defender pushed him.
Well, it seems unfair. Al-Nassr played much better in the first half.
Maybe, but they missed so many chances.

p2.t: So who do you think will win the league this year?
The way I see it, Al-Hilal has the strongest team, so they deserve to win.
I'm not sure. In my opinion, the league is very close this season.
We'll see! Quick, the second half is starting.

dialogue.focus: The way I see it, Al-Hilal has the strongest team, so they deserve to win.

dialogue.scene: Reem lives in Riyadh. Her friend Lama lives in a small town in Qassim. They are talking on a video call.

p1.t: Lama, what do you think about living in a small town?
I love it. It's peaceful, and my grandparents live next door.
It seems to me that small towns are a bit boring. In Riyadh there's a lot to do.
That's true, but Riyadh is so crowded. How long does it take you to get to school?

p2.t: About forty minutes, because of the traffic jams every morning.
Forty minutes! I walk to school in five.
OK, you win! But we have Riyadh Season, the Boulevard and huge malls.
I'm not sure, but I think a small town is still better for me. I'll visit you in winter, though!

dialogue.focus: It seems to me that small towns are a bit boring.

dialogue.scene: Students are recording a show for the school radio. Today's question is: 'Should students get homework every day?' Sultan is the presenter, and Majed is his guest.

p1.t: Welcome to School Radio! Should we get homework every day? Majed, what's your view on this?
From my point of view, a little homework every day makes sense. It helps us remember the lesson.
But many students say it's a waste of time. What do you think about that?
To be honest, some homework is boring. But the main reason we need it is practice.

p2.t: Some parents say their children feel too much pressure. Is that true?
Sometimes, yes, especially before exams. If you ask me, twenty minutes a day is enough.
Interesting! So you're not against homework?
No. I'm convinced that short homework is better than no homework at all.

dialogue.focus: From my point of view, a little homework every day makes sense.
qs: Why does Majed think homework makes sense?
How much homework is enough, in Majed's opinion?

speakout.scene: You're a guest on the school radio show, and I'm the presenter. Today's question is: 'Should students be allowed to bring phones to school?' Give your opinions with reasons, and ask for mine too.

prompts.q: What's your view on phones at school?

dialogue.scene: Faisal and Omar are choosing what to eat at a food court in a mall in Dammam.

p1.t: I'm in the mood for kabsa. I love the chicken kabsa here.
So do I! It's the best kabsa in Dammam.
But I don't like it when the sauce is too spicy.
Neither do I. Last time my mouth was on fire!

p2.t: What about dessert? I really like kunafa.
Really? I don't. It's too sweet for me. I prefer ice cream.
I can't believe it! Everyone likes kunafa.
Well, it's just a matter of taste. My sister feels the same way.
OK, fair enough. Let's order the kabsa and decide on dessert later.

dialogue.focus: So do I! It's the best kabsa in Dammam.

So have I. Let's choose Abha this time. The cool weather there is amazing.

p2.t: We could go camping in the mountains near Abha.
I'm not keen on that. I can't sleep well in a tent.
Neither can I, to be honest! Let's stay in a hotel and go camping for one night only.

dialogue.scene: Reem and her classmate Emma are talking about last week's online lessons.

p1.t: I loved the online lessons last week. I could learn in my pyjamas!
Ha! I see your point, but I couldn't concentrate at all.
Why not? It was so quiet at home.
Not in my house! My little brothers were a big distraction.

p2.t: OK, you've got a point. But we didn't waste time in traffic.
That's true, but I missed my friends. I prefer learning face to face.
To be honest, I feel the same way. Seeing everyone at school is more fun.
So online lessons are good sometimes, but not every day.

dialogue.focus: I see your point, but I couldn't concentrate at all.

speakout.scene: You've invented a new gadget for kids. I'm a judge at the school science fair. Describe your invention to me in detail.

prompts.q: What's your invention?
prompts.hint: Say 'It's a gadget which / that …'.

prompts.q: What is it used for?
prompts.hint: Use 'It's used for …ing' and give an example.

prompts.q: When will it come in handy?
prompts.hint: Describe a situation and say who it will help.

culture.title: Inventions from the Arab World
points: Al-Jazari, a famous inventor from about 800 years ago, designed amazing water clocks and machines.
The Arab scientist Ibn al-Haytham did important work on light and how our eyes see.
Today, Saudi universities like KAUST work on inventions for clean water and energy.
qs: Which invention do you think changed the world the most?
What gadget would you like someone to invent?

3-1.exit: Describe your favourite gadget in two sentences. Use 'which' or 'that' at least once.

3-2.objective: Today you will describe interesting places in detail using 'where'.
3-2.warmup: What's the most beautiful place you've ever visited?

expressions.def: important in history
expressions.frame: ___ is a historic place in my country.

expressions.def: to be known by many people for something
expressions.frame: My city is famous for ___.

expressions.def: very beautiful or exciting
expressions.frame: The view from ___ is breathtaking.

expressions.def: very, very old
expressions.frame: I'd love to see the ancient ___ in ___.

expressions.def: to be good enough that you should go there
expressions.frame: ___ is really worth a visit.

expressions.def: a person who travels to visit places for fun
expressions.frame: Lots of tourists visit ___ every year.

dialogue.scene: Omar has just come back from a family trip to AlUla. He shows some photos to his friend Sam.

p1.t: Where are these photos from, Omar?
AlUla! This is Hegra, the place where the Nabataeans built huge tombs in the rocks.
Wow, it looks ancient! How old is it?
About two thousand years old. It's a historic site, and it's famous for those tombs.

p2.t: And what's this? It looks like an elephant!
That's Elephant Rock, the place where we watched the sunset. The view was breathtaking.
Are there many tourists there?
Yes, lots, especially in winter. If you ask me, AlUla is really worth a visit.

dialogue.focus: This is Hegra, the place where the Nabataeans built huge tombs in the rocks.
qs: What is Hegra famous for?
What did Omar's family do at Elephant Rock?

speakout.scene: I'm a tourist visiting Saudi Arabia for the first time. I'm asking you, a local, about places to visit.

prompts.q: Which place in Saudi Arabia is really worth a visit?
prompts.hint: Name it and describe it with 'It's a place where …'.

prompts.q: What is your city or town famous for?
prompts.hint: Give two things and add details with 'where' or 'which'.

prompts.q: Where's the best place to watch the sunset?
prompts.hint: Describe it with adjectives like breathtaking or peaceful.

culture.title: UNESCO Sites in Saudi Arabia
points: In 2008, Hegra became the first place in Saudi Arabia on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
At-Turaif in Diriyah is the place where the first Saudi state began.
Al-Ahsa Oasis, where there are millions of palm trees, is also on the list.
qs: Which of these places would you like to visit? Why?
Why do you think it's important to protect historic places?

3-2.exit: Describe a place you love in two sentences. Use 'where' in one of them.

3-3.objective: Today you will describe people in your family or class using 'whose' and other details.
3-3.warmup: Who do you look like in your family?

expressions.def: to know who someone is because you have seen them before
expressions.frame: I didn't recognise ___ at first.

expressions.def: to look or act like an older person in your family
expressions.frame: I take after my ___ because we both ___.

expressions.def: to look the same as each other
expressions.frame: ___ and ___ look alike.

expressions.def: a funny or friendly name that people call you
expressions.frame: My nickname is ___ because ___.

expressions.def: having lots of curls
expressions.frame: The person in my family with curly hair is ___.

expressions.def: being the person who controls or looks after something
expressions.frame: In my house, ___ is in charge of ___.

dialogue.scene: Faisal is showing his friend Daniel an old family photo at his grandfather's house.

p1.t: Who are all these people, Faisal?
My family, twenty years ago! That's my grandfather, the man whose camel won a race.
Ha! And who's the boy with curly hair? I don't recognise him.
That's my dad! He was ten. People say I take after him.

p2.t: You really look alike! And who are the two boys whose shirts are the same?
Twins! My uncles Fahad and Faris. Their nickname was 'Copy and Paste'.
That's funny! Who's the man in charge of the barbecue?
My great-uncle Saad. He's the one whose stories everyone loves.

dialogue.focus: That's my grandfather, the man whose camel won a race.
qs: Why doesn't Daniel recognise the boy with curly hair?
What was the twins' nickname?

speakout.scene: Let's play a guessing game. Think of someone in your family or class. Describe them using 'whose', 'who' and other details, and I'll guess.

prompts.q: Tell me about the person's family or the things they own.
prompts.hint: Use 'It's someone whose …' (for example, whose brother is a pilot).

prompts.q: Who do they take after in their family?
prompts.hint: Say who they look like or act like.

prompts.q: Do they have a nickname?
prompts.hint: Say the nickname and explain where it comes from.

culture.title: Names Around the World
points: In Saudi Arabia, many fathers are called 'Abu' + their oldest son's name, like Abu Fahad.
In Iceland, many family names are the father's first name + 'son' or 'dóttir'.
In China, the family name comes first and the given name comes second.
qs: Do you have a nickname? Who gave it to you?
Who in your family do you take after?

3-3.exit: Describe two people you know in two sentences. Use 'whose' in both of them.

3-4.objective: Today you will describe a lost thing and the place where you lost it in detail.
3-4.warmup: Have you ever lost something important?

expressions.def: to forget to take something with you
expressions.frame: I once left my ___ behind at ___.

expressions.def: used to say what material something is
expressions.frame: My ___ is made of ___.

expressions.def: completely new
expressions.frame: My ___ is brand-new.

expressions.def: a design of lines, shapes or colours
expressions.frame: My favourite ___ has a pattern of ___.

expressions.def: to be owned by someone
expressions.frame: This ___ belongs to ___.

expressions.def: a place where people take things that others have lost
expressions.frame: If I lose my ___, I'll ask at the lost and found.

dialogue.scene: Ali left his backpack on the metro in Riyadh. He is at the lost and found office, talking to an officer, Mr Nasser.

p1.t: Good morning. Welcome to the lost and found. How can I help you?
I left my backpack behind on the metro this morning. It was on the train which left Olaya at eight.
OK. Can you describe it?
It's a brand-new blue backpack which has a pattern of white stars. It's made of soft material.

p2.t: What was inside it?
My school books and a lunch box that my mum bought in Turkey. It has my name on it.
A man whose son was on the same train brought this one in. Is it yours?
Yes, that's it! It belongs to me. Thank you so much!
You're welcome. Please check everything's there, and sign here.

dialogue.focus: It's a brand-new blue backpack which has a pattern of white stars.
qs: What does Ali's backpack look like?
Who brought the backpack to the office?

speakout.scene: You've lost something important at the airport. I work at the lost and found office. Describe the thing and the place where you lost it in detail.

prompts.q: What did you lose, and what does it look like?
prompts.hint: Give the colour, size, pattern and what it's made of. Use 'which'.

prompts.q: Where do you think you left it behind?
prompts.hint: Describe the place with 'where' (for example, the café where I had breakfast).

prompts.q: How do I know it belongs to you?
prompts.hint: Describe something inside it or something special about it, using 'which' or 'that'.

culture.title: Lost Things Around the World
points: In Tokyo, people take millions of lost things to the police every year.
Some airports use special computer systems to find the owners of lost bags.
During Hajj, special teams help pilgrims who have lost their bags or their way.
qs: Have you ever left something behind? What happened?
What should you do if you find someone's wallet?

3-4.exit: Describe one thing you own in two sentences, so that someone can find it if you lose it. Use 'which' or 'that'.

3-5.objective: Today you will show a visitor around your city and describe people, places and things in detail.
3-5.warmup: What's the first place you'd show a visitor in your city?

expressions.def: found in a particular place
expressions.frame: My school is located in ___.

expressions.def: a famous building or place that is easy to recognise
expressions.frame: The most famous landmark in my city is ___.

expressions.def: having things all around
expressions.frame: My grandparents' farm is surrounded by ___.

expressions.def: from the area where you live
expressions.frame: A famous local dish in my city is ___.

expressions.def: the best or most exciting part of something
expressions.frame: The highlight of my last trip was ___.

expressions.def: something you buy to remember a place
expressions.frame: A good souvenir from my city is ___.

dialogue.scene: Hamad is a young volunteer guide in Riyadh. He is showing a visitor from Japan, Kenji, around the city.

p1.t: Welcome to Riyadh, Kenji! That tall tower is the Kingdom Centre, the most famous landmark in the city.
It's amazing! What's at the top?
A sky bridge which gives you a view of the whole city.
Great! What else should I see?

p2.t: Diriyah, which is located on the edge of the city. It's the place where the first Saudi state began.
What's the highlight there?
At-Turaif, an old district which is surrounded by mud-brick walls. Then we'll try some local food.
Perfect! And where can I buy a souvenir for my family?
Souq Al-Zal, where you can find old coins, carpets and Arabic coffee pots.

dialogue.focus: It's the place where the first Saudi state began.
qs: What can you see from the sky bridge?
What can Kenji buy at Souq Al-Zal?

speakout.scene: You're a tour guide in your own city or town. I'm a visitor from another country. Show me around and describe everything in detail.

prompts.q: What's the most famous landmark here?
prompts.hint: Name it and describe it with 'which' or 'where'.

prompts.q: Who are the people who make this place special?
prompts.hint: Describe local people or a famous person with 'who' or 'whose'.

prompts.q: What's a good souvenir, and where can I buy it?
prompts.hint: Describe the thing and the shop or market with 'which' and 'where'.

culture.title: Famous Landmarks
points: The Kingdom Centre in Riyadh is about 300 metres tall.
The King Fahd Fountain in Jeddah sends water more than 250 metres into the air.
The Eiffel Tower in Paris, which was built in 1889, is visited by millions of people every year.
qs: Which landmark would you show a visitor first? Why?
What's the best souvenir from Saudi Arabia, in your opinion?

3-5.exit: In two sentences, describe your city to a visitor. Use 'which', 'where' or 'who'.

words.ex: In my opinion, chess is more exciting than people think.
This puzzle game is so addictive that I forgot to eat lunch.
My dad thinks watching other people play games is a waste of time.
My mum checks my screen time every evening.
To be honest, I found the new game a bit boring.
What do you think about playing games online with strangers?

dialogue.t: Omar, that's three hours on that game! What do you think about your screen time today?
To be honest, it's a bit too much. But this new football game is really addictive.
In my opinion, three hours is a waste of time. It's a beautiful day outside.
Maybe, but it isn't a complete waste. I'm learning to work with my team online.
That's interesting. What do you think about playing real football instead?
Well, I think real football is better for my health, because I actually move.
Exactly. So let's go to the park after Asr. Dad can take us.
Fine! I'll save the game and come with you.

grammar.title: Giving opinions: I think / In my opinion
grammar.ar: نستخدم I think أو In my opinion قبل رأينا، ونضيف because لذكر السبب. وللسؤال عن رأي غيرنا: What do you think about + اسم أو فعل بـ ing؟
examples: I think this game is too difficult for young children.
In my opinion, reading is better than watching TV.
What do you think about playing games online?

words.ex: Personally, I prefer homemade sandwiches to canteen food.
I'm not keen on spicy food, but my brother loves it.
Fruit salad is a healthy option for break time.
What's your opinion of the new school timetable?
I believe that every student should drink more water.
The soup was tasteless, so nobody finished it.

dialogue.t: Noura, what's your opinion of the new canteen menu?
Personally, I'm not keen on it. The pasta was tasteless yesterday.
Really? I liked the chicken wrap. I believe it's a healthy option too.
Maybe, but they stopped selling samosas! That's a real shame.
In my opinion, it's good that they sell less fried food.
I suppose so. But I believe students should be able to choose.
What do you think about writing to the head teacher about it?
That's a great idea! Let's ask her to add fresh juice and dates.

grammar.title: Personally / I believe that / What's your opinion of …?
grammar.ar: Personally تعني رأيي أنا. بعد I believe نضع (that) + جملة كاملة. وWhat's your opinion of + اسم؟ سؤال مهذب عن الرأي.
examples: Personally, I love the canteen's falafel.
I believe that students need longer breaks.
What's your opinion of the new uniform?

words.ex: What did you think of the football match last night?
I found the book quite hard at first, but then I loved it.
Everyone loves that series, but I think it's overrated.
The plot was so confusing that I watched it twice.
How do you feel about films with sad endings?
The new animated film is worth watching with your family.

dialogue.t: So, Faisal, what did you think of the film?
I found it really funny, but the plot was a bit confusing in the middle.
Really? I thought the plot was clever. The ending surprised me.
True, the ending was great. But was the first film better?
To be honest, I think the first one is a bit overrated. This one was better.
I'm not sure. How do you feel about films with so many songs?
I usually skip the songs at home! But overall, it was worth watching.
In my opinion, it's the best film this year. Let's tell everyone at school!

grammar.title: Asking for opinions: What did you think of …? / How do you feel about …?
grammar.ar: بعد تجربة شيء نسأل: What did you think of …؟ وعن الشعور العام: How do you feel about …؟ والإجابة: I found it + صفة.
examples: What did you think of the new series?
How do you feel about very long films?
I found the ending really exciting.

words.ex: If you ask me, that was the best goal of the season.
The way I see it, the team needs a faster goalkeeper.
They didn't deserve to win; they only had one shot on goal.
It's unfair that the older boys always choose the teams.
The referee gave a yellow card to their captain.
Who do you think will score first tonight?

dialogue.t: That was never a penalty! The referee made a terrible mistake.
If you ask me, it was a penalty. The defender pushed him.
Well, it seems unfair. Al-Nassr played much better in the first half.
Maybe, but they missed so many chances.
So who do you think will win the league this year?
The way I see it, Al-Hilal has the strongest team, so they deserve to win.
I'm not sure. In my opinion, the league is very close this season.
We'll see! Quick, the second half is starting.

grammar.title: Strong opinions: If you ask me / The way I see it
grammar.ar: عبارات لإبداء رأي قوي، تأتي في أول الجملة ثم فاصلة ثم الرأي. وللسؤال عن التوقع: Who do you think will + فعل؟
examples: If you ask me, the coach should change the team.
The way I see it, they played better in the second half.
Who do you think will win the cup?

words.ex: It seems to me that our town needs more parks.
The mall was so crowded that we went home early.
My grandfather's farm is very peaceful in the evening.
There was a huge traffic jam after the match.
I'm not sure, but I think the new park opens next week.
There's a lot to do in Jeddah, like swimming and visiting old Al-Balad.

dialogue.t: Lama, what do you think about living in a small town?
I love it. It's peaceful, and my grandparents live next door.
It seems to me that small towns are a bit boring. In Riyadh there's a lot to do.
That's true, but Riyadh is so crowded. How long does it take you to get to school?
About forty minutes, because of the traffic jams every morning.
Forty minutes! I walk to school in five.
OK, you win! But we have Riyadh Season, the Boulevard and huge malls.
I'm not sure, but I think a small town is still better for me. I'll visit you in winter, though!

grammar.title: Careful opinions: It seems to me that … / I'm not sure, but …
grammar.ar: It seems to me that تعطي رأياً بلطف وحذر. ونقول I'm not sure, but I think … عندما لا نكون متأكدين من رأينا.
examples: It seems to me that the traffic is getting worse.
I'm not sure, but I think small towns are safer.
It seems to me that there isn't a lot to do here for teenagers.

words.ex: From my point of view, school should start a bit later.
I'm convinced that reading every day makes you smarter.
What's your view on longer school holidays?
It makes sense to do your homework before you play.
There's a lot of pressure on players before a final.
The main reason I walk to school is the exercise.

dialogue.t: Welcome to School Radio! Should we get homework every day? Majed, what's your view on this?
From my point of view, a little homework every day makes sense. It helps us remember the lesson.
But many students say it's a waste of time. What do you think about that?
To be honest, some homework is boring. But the main reason we need it is practice.
Some parents say their children feel too much pressure. Is that true?
Sometimes, yes, especially before exams. If you ask me, twenty minutes a day is enough.
Interesting! So you're not against homework?
No. I'm convinced that short homework is better than no homework at all.

grammar.title: Opinions with reasons
grammar.ar: نقوّي رأينا بذكر السبب: The main reason is … . ونسأل عن رأي الآخرين: What's your view on …? ونعبّر عن قناعة قوية: I'm convinced that … .
examples: From my point of view, the school day is too long.
The main reason is that we're tired after lunch.
What's your view on online homework?

words.ex: A: I love mango juice. B: So do I!
A: I don't eat fish. B: Neither do I.
This chicken is too spicy for my little sister.
I'm in the mood for something sweet after dinner.
Choosing a favourite colour is just a matter of taste.
My brother hates waiting, and I feel the same way.

dialogue.t: I'm in the mood for kabsa. I love the chicken kabsa here.
So do I! It's the best kabsa in Dammam.
But I don't like it when the sauce is too spicy.
Neither do I. Last time my mouth was on fire!
What about dessert? I really like kunafa.
Really? I don't. It's too sweet for me. I prefer ice cream.
I can't believe it! Everyone likes kunafa.
Well, it's just a matter of taste. My sister feels the same way.

grammar.title: So do I / Neither do I
grammar.ar: نوافق على جملة مثبتة بـ So do I، وعلى جملة منفية بـ Neither do I. وإذا اختلفنا نقول: Really? I don't. أو Really? I do.
examples: A: I like dates. B: So do I.
A: I don't eat fish. B: Neither do I.
A: I love kunafa. B: Really? I don't.

words.ex: A: I'm tired of this heat. B: So am I!
A: I can't swim very well. B: Neither can I.
A: I've visited Abha twice. B: So have I.
I can't wait to see my cousins at Eid.
We go to Taif in summer for the cool weather.
We go camping in the desert every winter.

dialogue.t: I'm so tired of the heat in Riyadh. I can't wait for the summer holidays!
So am I! Dad says we can choose between Abha and Jeddah.
Hmm. I've been to Jeddah twice already.
So have I. Let's choose Abha this time. The cool weather there is amazing.
We could go camping in the mountains near Abha.
I'm not keen on that. I can't sleep well in a tent.
Neither can I, to be honest! Let's stay in a hotel and go camping for one night only.
Good idea. I can't wait to tell Mum and Dad.

grammar.title: Short answers: So am I / Neither can I / So have I
grammar.ar: في الرد القصير نستخدم نفس الفعل المساعد الموجود في الجملة: am ← So am I، can't ← Neither can I، have ← So have I.
examples: A: I'm tired. B: So am I.
A: I can't ride a camel. B: Neither can I.
A: I've seen that film. B: So have I.

words.ex: I see your point, but I still think school is more fun.
That's true, but the trip is very expensive.
You've got a point. We should leave early to avoid traffic.
It's better to say sorry face to face, not by message.
I can concentrate better in the library.
The TV is a big distraction when I do homework.

dialogue.t: I loved the online lessons last week. I could learn in my pyjamas!
Ha! I see your point, but I couldn't concentrate at all.
Why not? It was so quiet at home.
Not in my house! My little brothers were a big distraction.
OK, you've got a point. But we didn't waste time in traffic.
That's true, but I missed my friends. I prefer learning face to face.
To be honest, I feel the same way. Seeing everyone at school is more fun.
So online lessons are good sometimes, but not every day.

grammar.title: Disagreeing politely
grammar.ar: لا نقول You're wrong! بل نوافق على جزء من الفكرة أولاً ثم نعرض رأينا: I see your point, but … / That's true, but … .
examples: I see your point, but I learn better at school.
That's true, but online lessons can be boring.
You've got a point. Maybe we can do both.

words.ex: I totally agree that we should eat together as a family.
I'm afraid I don't agree. I think the rule is too strict.
A: Pets need lots of love. B: Exactly!
My cousin takes care of his grandfather's camels.
Feeding the birds is my responsibility.
Please don't make a mess in the kitchen.

dialogue.t: Dad, can we get a cat? All my friends have one!
Hmm. A cat is a big responsibility, Sara.
I totally agree. That's why I'll take care of it every day.
Every day? Even during exams?
Yes! And I'll clean its box. It won't make a mess, I promise.
I'm afraid I don't agree. Cats often make a mess with their hair and toys.
That's true, but we can brush it every week.
Well, you've got a point. Let's ask your mum first. Her opinion matters too.

grammar.title: Strong agreement and polite disagreement
grammar.ar: للموافقة القوية: I totally agree / Exactly!. وللاعتراض بأدب: I'm afraid I don't agree. كلمة I'm afraid هنا تجعل الاعتراض ألطف.
examples: I totally agree with you.
Exactly! That's what I think.
I'm afraid I don't agree. Cats are easy to keep.

words.ex: I couldn't agree more. We need more trees in our city.
You may be right, but it's too hot to walk to school.
A: New phones are always better. B: Not necessarily.
Our school recycles paper and cans.
Turning off the lights can make a big difference.
Many shops have stopped giving single-use plastic bags.

dialogue.t: Look at all these plastic bottles! We should stop using single-use plastic.
I couldn't agree more. It's terrible for the fish and turtles.
But one small club can't make a difference.
You may be right, but if every school does this, it will help.
True. My family recycles paper and bottles now.
So does mine! But recycling isn't enough. We need to use less plastic.
Do you think paper bags are always better than plastic ones?
Not necessarily. If you ask me, bags you can use again and again are the best.

grammar.title: Agreeing and disagreeing in discussions
grammar.ar: I couldn't agree more = موافقة تامة. You may be right, but … = موافقة جزئية ثم اعتراض. Not necessarily = ليس دائماً صحيحاً.
examples: I couldn't agree more. Plastic is a big problem.
You may be right, but recycling is expensive.
A: Big cars are safer. B: Not necessarily.

words.ex: I'm with you on that. The zoo is perfect for younger students.

words.w: I'm not so sure about that.
words.ex: I'm not so sure about that. It might rain tomorrow.
Fair enough. Let's leave the beach for winter.
The majority of students voted for the museum.
I wanted the red bike, but then I changed my mind.
After a long talk, my brothers and I came to an agreement.

dialogue.t: OK, we have three choices: Ithra, the beach in Al-Khobar or a farm trip. What do you think?
Ithra, definitely. It has a library, a museum and a cinema.
I'm with you on that. But some students say it's boring.
I'm not so sure about that. They have fun science shows for kids.
The beach is fun too. Lots of students love swimming.
That's true, but it's very hot this month. We can go to the beach in winter.
Fair enough. Let's ask the class and see what the majority wants.
Good idea. And if they choose the farm, maybe I'll change my mind!

grammar.title: Reaching an agreement
grammar.ar: في النقاش نوافق (I'm with you on that)، ونشكّك بأدب (I'm not so sure about that)، ونقبل الرأي الآخر (Fair enough) حتى نصل إلى اتفاق.
examples: I'm with you on that. Ithra is a great choice.
I'm not so sure about that. The farm is very far.
Fair enough. Let's ask the majority.

words.ex: Khalid fell out with his cousin over a video game.
Why don't you call him and say sorry?
The twins argued in the morning but made up by lunch.
He apologised for being late to the match.
Have you tried talking to your teacher about it?
She was upset because nobody remembered her birthday.

dialogue.t: What's wrong, Omar? You look upset.
I fell out with Yousef. I laughed when he missed a penalty, and now he won't talk to me.
Oh no. Have you tried talking to him?
Yes, but he walked away. What should I do?
Why don't you apologise? Tell him you're really sorry you laughed.
But it was just a joke!
Maybe for you, but not for him. You could send him a message tonight.
OK, I'll try. I really want to make up with him before Thursday's match.

grammar.title: Making suggestions
grammar.ar: Why don't you + فعل؟ اقتراح لطيف. You could + فعل = يمكنك أن. Have you tried + فعل بـ ing؟ = هل جرّبت؟
examples: Why don't you invite him to play?
You could write her a short note.
Have you tried asking your teacher for help?

words.ex: If I were you, I'd start revising this weekend.
My sister gets stressed out before every exam.
I revise my English words on the bus.
Let's take a break and have some juice.
He was ill for a week and fell behind in science.
My mum helped me make a timetable for Ramadan.

dialogue.t: Hind, I'm so stressed out. I have four exams next week!
Don't worry, that's normal. Have you started to revise?
A bit, but I'm falling behind in maths. I don't know where to start.
If I were you, I'd make a timetable. Write which subject you'll study each day.
Good idea. But I study for hours and still forget everything.
Then take a break every forty minutes. Your brain needs rest.
Really? I thought breaks were a waste of time.
Not at all! And if I were you, I'd ask your teacher for extra maths exercises.

grammar.title: If I were you, I'd + verb
grammar.ar: عبارة ثابتة للنصيحة: If I were you (لاحظ were مع I) ثم I'd أو I wouldn't + فعل في صيغته الأساسية.
examples: If I were you, I'd go to bed early.
If I were you, I wouldn't study all night.
If I were you, I'd ask the teacher.

words.ex: Children need to get enough sleep to grow well.
We stayed up late on the last night of Ramadan.
There's too much junk food in my lunch box.
After the long match, the players were exhausted.
I've got into the habit of drinking water before school.
Saving a little money every week will help you in the long run.

dialogue.t: Faisal, you look exhausted. Are you OK?
I stayed up late again, sir. I was playing online with my cousins.
If you don't get enough sleep, you won't play well in the match on Thursday.
I know. But I can't fall asleep early. I'm not tired at ten.
Why don't you put your phone away an hour before bed? You'll fall asleep faster.
OK. And what about breakfast? I usually just eat crisps.
That's junk food! If you eat eggs or labneh and bread, you'll have more energy.
Fine, I'll try to get into the habit of eating a proper breakfast.

grammar.title: First conditional for advice
grammar.ar: If + مضارع بسيط، ثم will أو won't + فعل: نستخدمه لنشرح نتيجة النصيحة في المستقبل. لا نضع will بعد If.
examples: If you go to bed early, you'll feel better.
If you eat junk food every day, you won't have much energy.
You'll get stronger if you exercise every day.

words.ex: My brother is saving up for a new bike.
I get my pocket money every Thursday.
You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the bus.
We can't afford a new car this year.
These shoes were a bargain. They were half price!
You won't finish your project unless you start today.

dialogue.t: Look at those football boots, Uncle! But they cost 400 riyals. I can't afford them.
How much pocket money do you get?
Fifty riyals a week, but I usually spend it all on snacks and games.
Well, you'd better stop that if you really want those boots.
So, what should I do?
It's a good idea to save up for them. If you save forty riyals a week, you'll have enough in ten weeks.
Ten weeks! That's so long.
Maybe, but you won't get them unless you save. And wait for the sale. They might be a bargain then.

grammar.title: You'd better / It's a good idea to / unless
grammar.ar: You'd better + فعل = نصيحة قوية (وإلا ستحدث مشكلة). It's a good idea to + فعل = نصيحة لطيفة. unless = إلا إذا (أي if not).
examples: You'd better save some money every week.
It's a good idea to compare prices first.
You won't have enough money unless you save.

words.ex: Can I ask your advice about my science project?
I want to learn to cook. What do you suggest?
My advice is to arrive early on your first day.
It took my cousin a month to fit in at his new school.
I'm getting used to waking up early.
I always feel nervous before I speak in front of the class.

dialogue.t: Noura, can I ask your advice? I start at my new school on Sunday.
Of course! Are you nervous?
Very! I don't know anyone, and I'm worried I won't fit in.
Don't worry. My advice is to join a club. You'll meet people who like the same things.
Good idea. And what do you suggest for the weekend? Everything is so different here.
Why don't you come with us to Diriyah on Friday evening? It's beautiful at night.
I'd love to! But the weekend is on Friday and Saturday here. It feels so strange.
You'll get used to it quickly, I promise!

grammar.title: Asking for advice
grammar.ar: نطلب النصيحة بأدب: Can I ask your advice? / What do you suggest? / What should I do? والرد يكون: My advice is to + فعل.
examples: Can I ask your advice about something?
I'm nervous about the test. What do you suggest?
My advice is to practise every day.

words.ex: My dad knows how to deal with difficult customers.
Whatever you do, don't tell him about the surprise!
It might help to write your new words in a notebook.
I nearly gave up, but then I scored a goal.
We lost the match, but look on the bright side: we played well.

dialogue.t: Welcome back to 'Ask Us'! Today's message is from Turki, who's 11. He says: 'I'm terrible at swimming, and my friends laugh at me.'
Poor Turki! Well, Turki, whatever you do, don't give up.
I agree. It might help to take lessons at a sports club. If you practise every week, you'll improve quickly.
And look on the bright side: you're trying something new, and that's brave.
What about his friends? How should he deal with them?
If I were you, Turki, I'd tell them how you feel. Real friends will understand.
Exactly. Why don't you invite them to practise with you? You could sort it out together.
Great advice! Send us your problems, everyone, and we'll try to help.

grammar.title: Gentle and strong advice
grammar.ar: نصيحة لطيفة: It might help to … / You could … . نصيحة قوية: You'd better … / Whatever you do, don't … . ونذكر النتيجة بـ If you …, you'll … .
examples: It might help to make a list.
Whatever you do, don't give up.
If you practise every day, you'll get better.

words.ex: I look up to my grandfather because he's so wise.
The captain is a great role model for young players.
My mum is a hard-working nurse.
Our neighbour is generous. He shares his dates with everyone.

dialogue.t: Ali, who are you going to talk about in the presentation?
My uncle Hamad. He's the person who taught me to swim.
Cool! Why do you look up to him?
He's a doctor who works in a village hospital. He's so hard-working and generous.
My role model is Rayyanah Barnawi. She's the scientist who went to space in 2023.
Wow! She was the first Saudi woman who travelled to space, right?
Exactly. She achieved her dream, and she inspires lots of young people.
Great choice! I think our presentations will be the best in the class.

grammar.title: Relative clauses with who
grammar.ar: نستخدم who بعد اسم شخص مباشرة لنضيف معلومة عنه: She's the scientist who went to space. ولا نضع he أو she بعد who.
examples: My uncle is a doctor who works in a village.
She's the teacher who helped me most.
People who read a lot know many words.

words.ex: My dad loves gadgets, like his smart watch.

dialogue.t: Look at this gadget! It's a robot which cleans solar panels in the desert.
Clever! Sand covers the panels all the time, so it really comes in handy.
Exactly. And it has a battery that charges in the sun.
What's that over there? It looks like a high-tech hat.
It's a helmet which is used for teaching people to drive. You see the road on a screen.
Wow! What's the best invention that you've ever seen?
Maybe the phone. It's a camera, a map and a computer at the same time.
True! But I'd say the air conditioner. Life in Riyadh in summer is impossible without it!

grammar.title: Relative clauses with which / that
grammar.ar: نستخدم which أو that بعد اسم شيء أو حيوان لنضيف معلومة عنه: a robot which cleans panels. ويمكن استخدام that للأشخاص والأشياء.
examples: It's a robot which cleans windows.

A fridge is a machine which keeps food cold.

dialogue.t: Where are these photos from, Omar?
AlUla! This is Hegra, the place where the Nabataeans built huge tombs in the rocks.
Wow, it looks ancient! How old is it?
About two thousand years old. It's a historic site, and it's famous for those tombs.
And what's this? It looks like an elephant!
That's Elephant Rock, the place where we watched the sunset. The view was breathtaking.
Are there many tourists there?
Yes, lots, especially in winter. If you ask me, AlUla is really worth a visit.

grammar.title: Relative clauses with where
grammar.ar: نستخدم where بعد اسم مكان لنصف ما يحدث فيه: the place where we watched the sunset. بعد where تأتي جملة كاملة (فاعل + فعل).
examples: This is the park where I learned to ride a bike.
Jeddah is the city where my grandparents live.
That's the café where we had breakfast.

words.ex: I didn't recognise my cousin with his new haircut.
My brother takes after my dad. They both love football.
My twin cousins look alike, but they're very different.
His nickname at school is 'The Professor'.

dialogue.t: Who are all these people, Faisal?
My family, twenty years ago! That's my grandfather, the man whose camel won a race.
Ha! And who's the boy with curly hair? I don't recognise him.
That's my dad! He was ten. People say I take after him.
You really look alike! And who are the two boys whose shirts are the same?
Twins! My uncles Fahad and Faris. Their nickname was 'Copy and Paste'.
That's funny! Who's the man in charge of the barbecue?
My great-uncle Saad. He's the one whose stories everyone loves.

grammar.title: Relative clauses with whose
grammar.ar: whose تعني (الذي/التي ... له/لها) وتدل على الملكية: the man whose camel won = الرجل الذي فاز جَمَله. بعد whose يأتي اسم مباشرة.
examples: He's the boy whose dad is a pilot.
She's the teacher whose class won the prize.
That's the man whose car broke down.

words.ex: I left my jacket behind at my cousin's house.
This bag is made of leather.

dialogue.t: Good morning. Welcome to the lost and found. How can I help you?
I left my backpack behind on the metro this morning. It was on the train which left Olaya at eight.
OK. Can you describe it?
It's a brand-new blue backpack which has a pattern of white stars. It's made of soft material.
What was inside it?
My school books and a lunch box that my mum bought in Turkey. It has my name on it.
A man whose son was on the same train brought this one in. Is it yours?
Yes, that's it! It belongs to me. Thank you so much!

grammar.title: Describing things in detail
grammar.ar: نصف الشيء بالصفات (الحجم ثم اللون) والمادة (made of) والنقشة (pattern)، ثم نضيف جملة which/that: a small black wallet which has my name inside.
examples: It's a small black wallet which has my name inside.
It's a bag that is made of leather.
I left it in the café where I had lunch.

words.ex: The museum is located in the old part of the city.
The Kingdom Centre is a famous Riyadh landmark.
The old town is surrounded by high walls.
We bought honey from a local farmer.
The highlight of the day was the camel ride.
I bought a small coffee pot as a souvenir.

dialogue.t: Welcome to Riyadh, Kenji! That tall tower is the Kingdom Centre, the most famous landmark in the city.
It's amazing! What's at the top?
A sky bridge which gives you a view of the whole city.
Great! What else should I see?
Diriyah, which is located on the edge of the city. It's the place where the first Saudi state began.
What's the highlight there?
At-Turaif, an old district which is surrounded by mud-brick walls. Then we'll try some local food.
Perfect! And where can I buy a souvenir for my family?

grammar.title: Mixing relative clauses
grammar.ar: who للأشخاص، which/that للأشياء، where للأماكن، whose للملكية. ونضع فاصلة قبل which إذا كانت معلومة إضافية: Diriyah, which is near Riyadh, … .
examples: Diriyah, which is near Riyadh, is very old.
